result.summary: Aborts node reindexing with a fatal error if the genesis block read from disk has a valid header but an invalid body. This avoids leaving the block index in an inconsistent state where the genesis header is accepted without an active chain, which previously caused either an assertion failure in CheckBlockIndex or a hang in RPC warmup.
result.problem: When reindexing corrupted block files where the genesis block has a valid header but an invalid body, reindexing accepts the header into the block index and attempts to continue. With -checkblockindex enabled (default on regtest), the node crashes on an assertion failure in CheckBlockIndex because multiple block headers exist without an active chain; without -checkblockindex, the node hangs indefinitely in RPC warmup.
evidence: Author description: "With -checkblockindex, the default on regtest, it aborts on an assert in CheckBlockIndex. Without it, it stays in RPC warmup."
Commit message: "CheckBlockIndex asserts that an index without an active chain has at most one entry. Without it, the node stays in RPC warmup."
result.scope_notes: The patch is small (+31/-0 across 2 files) and consists of the fatal error check during reindex plus a new functional test case in test/functional/feature_reindex.py.
result.card: Halts reindexing with a fatal error if the genesis block body read from disk is invalid. When reindexing corrupted data with a valid genesis header but invalid payload, nodes previously crashed on a CheckBlockIndex assertion (the default on regtest) or hung indefinitely in RPC warmup. The author provides a reproducible test case in feature_reindex.py flipping a bit in the genesis block.
uncertainties: The patch diff and file list were not provided in the prompt, so the exact error handling mechanism and validation file touched cannot be verified directly.

risk.why: A mistake in reindex block processing or fatal error handling could cause nodes to fail prematurely during reindex on valid or recoverable block storage.
